about: The words of the set-up's TMDB key, language, Usenet server, no-VPN and audio description questions, the API keys and Storage page steps, and the Updates step (DASH-178, DASH-189, DASH-183, DASH-131, DASH-399, DASH-417). The browser set-up (web/js/install.js) and the terminal set-up (starboard/setup_answers.py) both read this file, so they ask the same questions in the same order and words.

tmdb.title: Films and series information
tmdb.intro: Reelix finds each film and series, its posters and its episodes, in The Movie Database (TMDB). A free key lets it find far more, more accurately. Without one it uses open data and matches fewer titles.
tmdb.how: Get one free: make an account at themoviedb.org, then Settings, API, and copy the API Read Access Token (the long one) or the API key.
tmdb.question: TMDB key
tmdb.hint: Paste the API Read Access Token or the API key. Leave it empty to add it later in Settings, Reelix.
tmdb.skipped: No key for now: Reelix uses open data. Add one later in Settings, Reelix.

language.title: Language of releases
language.intro: Some releases are dubbed into another language. Reelix can skip those.
language.question: Which language should films and series be in?

choices.label: English (recommended)
choices.hint: Reelix skips releases in other languages.

choices.label: The film's or series' own language
choices.hint: Reelix gets each one in the language it was made in, with subtitles from Bazarr.

choices.label: Any language
choices.hint: Reelix takes the best release whatever its language.

usenet.server_intro: Type your provider's server details. They are in the email or account page your provider gave you.
usenet.port_hint: 563 for an encrypted connection, the usual choice; 119 without encryption
usenet.connections_hint: How many your plan allows, such as 20. Fewer is fine.
usenet.later: Starboard writes these into {app} once the apps are running.

novpn.title: Torrents without a VPN
novpn.text: Without a VPN, other people sharing the same torrents can see your home internet address, and your internet provider can see what you download. Usenet over SSL hides what you download from your internet provider, but your Usenet provider still sees it.
novpn.back: Go back and add a VPN (recommended)
novpn.browser: Tick VPN to add one, or choose Continue again to carry on without one.
novpn.question: How should your downloads connect?
novpn.use_about: Downloads go through your VPN, so your internet provider and other people sharing torrents see only the VPN.
novpn.without_about: Downloads use your home internet address. You can add a VPN later in Settings, Downloads, VPN.
warning: Without a VPN, other people sharing the same torrents can see your home internet address, and your internet provider can see what you download.
Where downloading something is not allowed, this can lead to warning letters from your internet provider or to legal action.
Usenet over SSL hides what you download from your internet provider, but your Usenet provider still sees it.
You can add a VPN later in Settings, Downloads, VPN.
novpn.confirm: I understand, continue without a VPN
novpn.chosen: You chose to download without a VPN.
novpn.reminder: Your internet provider and other people sharing torrents can see your home internet address and what you download.

docker.intro: Starboard can start, update and change your apps itself, and move the apps you already run, if it can use Docker. Docker access is full control of Docker, and so of this computer, so anyone who can sign in to Starboard could use it. Keep your Starboard password safe.
docker.without: Without it, Starboard still shows and checks your apps, but each change in Your install, each update and each move needs a command in a terminal on the server.
docker.move: Moving the apps you already run needs it: Starboard stops them, starts the new ones and moves their settings.
docker.no: No, I will run the commands myself
docker.done: The installer gives Starboard Docker access when it runs next (./install.sh --docker).

move.into: Move them into Reelix, and let Starboard run them (recommended)
move.into_about: Reelix takes over finding and sorting for Sonarr, Radarr and the rest, with their films, series, quality profiles and sites. Starboard then runs your apps, with a way back.
move.keep_about: Starboard only shows them on the dashboard. Move them later in Settings, Your install.
move.needs_docker: Moving needs Docker access, which Starboard gets when this set-up finishes. Then finish the move in Starboard, Settings, Your install, or run this set-up again.
move.waiting: Waiting for Reelix to finish setting up
move.hold: Hold the sites to search: only your old apps search until Starboard runs your apps

single_sign_on.label: Set up single sign-on
single_sign_on.hint: Recommended when other people use your apps: each person gets their own sign-in, and you keep the list in Settings, People. Leave it unticked on a server only you use, so nothing extra runs. It adds a plug-in, which you install in Settings, Plug-ins and which stays inactive until you turn it on. Its address is your server's Tailscale name, found in Tailscale's admin page. You choose the name once: passkeys are tied to it for ever, so changing it later makes every passkey stop working.
single_sign_on.chosen: Install Single sign-on in Settings, Plug-ins, Catalogue: check what it may do, then enter your password. Then choose its Tailscale name once.
single_sign_on.summary: single sign-on (to install in Settings, Plug-ins)
single_sign_on.notice_title: Single sign-on, chosen in the set-up
single_sign_on.notice_text: Install it here: check what it may do, then enter your password. It stays inactive until you turn it on. Choose its Tailscale name once: passkeys are tied to it for ever.
single_sign_on.coming: It is not in the plug-ins collection yet. Starboard offers it here once it is.
single_sign_on.later_done: Not now. Install single sign-on later in Settings, Plug-ins, Catalogue.

audio_description.label: Audio description
audio_description.hint: For blind and partially sighted people: a narrator says what happens on screen. Adds a plug-in that finds films and series with a described sound track and prefers them in Reelix. You install it in Settings, Plug-ins, and it stays inactive until you turn it on.
audio_description.chosen: Install Audio description in Settings, Plug-ins, Catalogue: check what it may do, then type your password.
audio_description.summary: audio description (to install in Settings, Plug-ins)
audio_description.notice_title: Audio description, chosen in the set-up
audio_description.notice_text: Install it here: check what it may do, then type your password. It stays inactive until you turn it on.
audio_description.coming: It is not in the plug-ins collection yet. Starboard offers it here once it is.
audio_description.later_done: Audio description is no longer offered here. Find it in the catalogue at any time.

keys.intro: With its key, Starboard can show an app's queue, calendar, updates and warnings. Each key stays on the server.

places.qbittorrent: Options, Web UI, API key (5.2 or later)

storage_page.intro: Sorting the space by type reads every file, so you choose when it happens. Everything here is also in Settings, General, Performance.
storage_page.usage_question: Work out what uses the space

usage.label: Only when I press Sort by type
When I open Storage, if over a day old

storage_page.refresh_hint: Sizes update by themselves while the page is open, or only when you press Check now.

refresh.label: Only when I press Check now

storage_page.daily_question: Keep a daily record of used space
storage_page.daily_hint: For the Space used over time chart and when the pool will be full. Nothing noticeable.

updates.intro: Starboard can install new versions by itself, in the update hours: your download hours when they are set, otherwise 01:00 to 06:00. Each part has a copy of its settings made first, is checked once it has updated, and goes back to the version before by itself if the new one does not start (Jellyfin's plug-ins cannot go back by themselves). You are told afterwards what is new, and when something failed.

parts.label: Starboard
parts.hint: Starboard restarts for about a minute. A version that did not install is not tried again until you update it yourself.

parts.label: Reelix
parts.hint: Once a day at most, with Reelix's settings saved first. Needs Docker access.

parts.label: Your other apps
parts.hint: Each app with a newer image, one at a time, with a copy of its settings first. Needs Docker access.

parts.label: Starboard plug-ins
parts.hint: From a catalogue or the plug-in's own address. A version that asks for new permissions always waits for you.

parts.label: Jellyfin's plug-ins
parts.hint: Jellyfin updates them in the update hours instead of on its own schedule, and restarts only when nobody is watching.

updates.later: Each is off unless you choose it. Change them later in Settings, Updates, where you can also choose the hours.
updates.saved: Saved. Change them later in Settings, Updates.

shadows.intro: Drop shadows cost a little processor on every scroll; turning them off helps small and older computers. They give cards, covers and menus some depth; borders stay, so nothing loses its edge.
shadows.lite: Reelix Lite is a light install, so it starts with the shadows removed.
shadows.full: This install starts with the shadows kept.
shadows.remove_about: Everything keeps its border; nothing else changes.
shadows.keep_about: Cards, covers and menus keep their shadow.
shadows.done_remove: Drop shadows are removed. Change it later in Display, Remove drop shadows.
shadows.done_keep: Drop shadows are kept. Change it later in Display, Remove drop shadows.
shadows.note: Drop shadows cost a little processor on every scroll; turning them off helps small and older computers
